curation.why: both *_body kinds are { } wrappers. Functions and initializers are named in breadcrumbs even where this sample doesn't nest declarations inside them. enum_entry is added as a landmark labelled `enum`, and `enum` as a container, matching the built-in profile codemark shipped before 0.8.0. The generator can never propose it: a case has no body and never wraps a declaration. Because this grammar parses `enum` as a class_declaration (labelled `class`), the `enum` container resolves only to enum_entry, which is what keeps a `case` line in the trail when an associated-value case or a long case list is bookmarked. subscript_declaration is labelled `subscript` — the generator proposes it as a landmark but leaves it unlabelled — and while_statement is labelled `while loop` purely so a query summary reads naturally.
